parts.html: Consulting a professional interior designer can transform even the smallest bathroom. Here are some key ideas and features that can be implemented:
Space Optimization:
Compact fixtures: Install smaller sinks, toilets, and showers to maximize usable space.
Wall-mounted elements: Wall-hung toilets and sinks create a sense of openness and make cleaning easier.
Color Palette and Lighting:
Dark tones: Even deep shades like graphite can visually enlarge a space.
Proper lighting: Recessed lights, backlit mirrors, LED strips under cabinets, or along the ceiling perimeter enhance brightness and ambiance.
Mirrors:
Large mirrors: Full-wall mirrors or large mirrored panels significantly expand visual space.
Storage:
Built-in cabinets: Maximize storage with custom-built units above the toilet or within walls.
Materials and Finishes:
Gloss vs. matte: Glossy finishes reflect light and make the room feel larger, while matte textures minimize maintenance.
Mosaic and tiles: Small-format mosaics or tiles create striking accents that distract from room size.
Décor:
Minimalism: Keep decorations to a minimum to avoid clutter.

Example implementation could include a light color palette, a large mirrored wall, wall-mounted fixtures, glossy tiles, and built-in storage — creating a sense of space and comfort even in the smallest bathroom.
